correctness.rationale: The four-letter state lift is checked from the binary adjacent-11 recurrence. Its eight source pairs form the complete substitution-closed pair language; extracting all length-eight windows yields disjoint 24-even and 32-odd factor sets. Injective two-letter images then yield the full 2-adic congruence synchronization lemma by induction. The dyadic five-block decomposition uses an exact high-bit XOR identity. The four boundary-pair comparisons rule out every first repetition before 4B, while the length-2B prefix repeats at 4B. All short lengths are explicitly checked. The packaged standard-library verifier reconstructs the finite critical certificate and exercises the formula but does not replace the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The initial non-repetitive complexity is an established, naturally motivated measure of how long an origin-anchored sequence avoids repeating contiguous factors. This theorem completely computes it for a canonical 2-automatic word, proves unique predecessor locations at first collision, and gives exact normalized liminf 2 and limsup 4. The proof exposes a nontrivial dyadic synchronization mechanism; it is not merely a finite recomputation, reparameterization or routine consequence of other automatic-word formulas.
